decision.summary: The Federal Reserve lowered its target for the federal funds rate by 50 basis points to 5-1/2 percent.

changes.quote: The Federal Open Market Committee at its meeting today decided to lower its target for the federal funds rate by 50 basis points to 5-1/2 percent.
changes.explanation: The Fed reduced its benchmark interest rate by a larger-than-usual 50 basis points to support the slowing economy.

changes.quote: Consumer and business confidence has eroded further, exacerbated by rising energy costs that continue to drain consumer purchasing power and press on business profit margins.
changes.explanation: The Fed noted that falling confidence and high energy costs are hurting consumers and businesses.

changes.quote: Partly as a consequence, retail sales and business spending on capital equipment have weakened appreciably.
changes.explanation: Weaker confidence has led to a slowdown in retail sales and business investments.

changes.quote: In response, manufacturing production has been cut back sharply, with new technologies appearing to have accelerated the response of production and demand to potential excesses in the stock of inventories and capital equipment.
changes.explanation: Manufacturers reduced production rapidly to prevent a buildup of unsold goods.

changes.quote: Taken together, and with inflation contained, these circumstances have called for a rapid and forceful response of monetary policy.
changes.explanation: Because inflation is under control, the Fed felt justified in taking swift action to protect the economy.

tone_quotes.quote: Consumer and business confidence has eroded further, exacerbated by rising energy costs that continue to drain consumer purchasing power and press on business profit margins.

Nonetheless, the Committee continues to believe that against the background of its long-run goals of price stability and sustainable economic growth and of the information currently available, the risks are weighted mainly toward conditions that may generate economic weakness in the foreseeable future.

for_you.text: On a $5,000 card balance at about 15.98% APR, a 50 bp cut lowers monthly interest by about $2.08.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 5.19% and moved -5 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 7.02% would fall by about $10.07 a month.
High-yield savings rates usually follow the Fed partly; on $10,000 that means roughly $30.00 a year less in interest.
Unemployment was 3.9%, and employers added an average of 126k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 3.4% over the past year (December 2000); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 1.9%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 2.4% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.

whats_next: The statement signals that the Federal Reserve remains highly focused on economic weakness and is prepared to adjust policy further if conditions warrant. Upcoming meetings will likely continue to evaluate whether additional rate cuts are needed to stabilize growth.
